items.markingKey: Draw both lines; they should cross at (3, 4), the algebraic solution. (R1 R1)

items.stem: Explain how many solutions the equations y = 3x + 6 and 9x − 3y = −18 have.
items.answer: The second rearranges to y = 3x + 6: the same line, so there are infinitely many solutions.
items.markingKey: Rearrange to compare gradients/intercepts (M1); The second rearranges to y = 3x + 6: the same line, so there are infinitely many solutions. (R1).

items.stem: A student claims that to solve x/3 + 2 = 5 you multiply only x/3 by 3 to get x + 2 = 5. Identify the error in this claim and correct it.
items.answer: Every term must be multiplied: x + 6 = 15, so x = 9.
items.markingKey: Every term must be multiplied: x + 6 = 15, so x = 9. 1 mark for identifying the error, 1-2 marks for the correct explanation.

items.stem: Explain why making r the subject of A = πr² gives r = √(A/π) and not r = A/π².
items.answer: Undo the operations in reverse: divide by π first, then undo squaring by taking the square root of A/π.
items.markingKey: Award marks for: Undo the operations in reverse: divide by π first, then undo squaring by taking the square root of A/π. (2 marks: one for each linked point in the chain of reasoning; no marks for assertion without explanation.)

items.stem: Explain why the inequalities x > 2 and 2 < x describe the same set of numbers.
items.answer: Both say x is to the right of 2 on the number line; reading an inequality from right to left reverses the symbol, not the meaning.
items.markingKey: Both say x is to the right of 2 on the number line; reading an inequality from right to left reverses the symbol, not the meaning. R1 A1.

items.stem: Chloé buys 5 notebooks and 1 pens for $64; Maya buys 2 notebooks and 4 pens for $40. Find the cost of one notebook and one pen.
items.answer: notebook $12, pen $4
items.markingKey: Variables defined and two equations formed (M1 A1); solved (M1); notebook $12, pen $4 (A1).

items.stem: Solve the simultaneous equations 3x + 4y = −2 and x − 4y = 26.
items.markingKey: Multiply to match coefficients and eliminate one unknown (M1); first value correct (A1); substitute back (M1); x = 6, y = −5 (A1).

items.stem: Solve 8x + 11 = 4x − 17.
items.markingKey: Collect x terms: 4x = −28 (M1 A1); x = −7 (A1).

items.stem: "If v = u + at, then t = v − u/a." Explain the flaw in this statement.
items.answer: Subtract u first, then divide the whole of (v − u) by a: t = (v − u)/a.
items.markingKey: Subtract u first, then divide the whole of (v − u) by a: t = (v − u)/a. 1 mark for identifying the error, 1-2 marks for the correct explanation.

items.stem: Solve −4x + 6 ≥ 4x + 56 and write the solution in interval notation.
items.markingKey: Collect x terms: -8x ≥ −56 (M1); divide by -8, reversing the sign (M1); x ≤ 7 and (−∞, 7] (A1 A1).

items.stem: The lines y = 2x + 2 and y = −2x + 10 are drawn on the same axes. Write down the coordinates of their point of intersection, and verify algebraically.
items.markingKey: Intersection (2, 6) (A1); verification: both equations give y = 6 when x = 2 (R1).

items.stem: Use substitution to solve y = 4x + 19 and 2x + 5y = 29.
A taxi charges a fixed fee of €9 plus €1.80 per km. Tariq paid €54.00. Write and solve an equation to find the distance travelled.
items.answer: 25 km
items.markingKey: Correct equation formed (M1 A1); solved correctly (M1); answer in context: 25 km (A1); check against the conditions (C1).

items.stem: The formula v = u + at gives the final speed of a cyclist. (a) Make a the subject. (b) Find a when u = 11 m/s, v = 31 m/s and t = 10 s.
items.answer: a = (v − u)/t; a = 2 m/s²
items.markingKey: Correct rearrangement (M1 A1); substitution (M1); a = (v − u)/t; a = 2 m/s² (A1).

items.stem: Find all integers x that satisfy both 2x − 3 > −7 and x + 6 ≤ 10, and represent them on a number line.
items.markingKey: Correct inequality (M1 A1); solved (M1); answer interpreted for whole numbers in context: −1, 0, 1, 2, 3, 4 (A1).

items.stem: A two-digit number has digits that add up to 11. When the digits are reversed, the new number is 45 more than the original. Find the number.
items.markingKey: Variables defined (C1); two correct equations (M1 A1); solved (M1); 38 with check in context (A1).
